summary: The bill requires the EPA, Interior, Energy, Agriculture, and Commerce departments to each create a 15-25 member Youth Advisory Council of people aged 16-29 (at least half from disadvantaged communities) that meets regularly and submits annual recommendations on environmental justice, climate impacts on youth, and related policies.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes $250,000 annually for each of five agencies (totaling $1.25 million per year) for fiscal years 2027–2037 to support the new Youth Advisory Councils and related administrative functions. This constitutes new federal spending on advisory bodies focused on environmental issues.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, credits, or revenue measures.
The bill addresses environmental advisory councils and has no connection to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
No provisions address firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill does not address immigration pathways, enforcement, or border policy.
No provisions relate to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill does not affect military or defense budgets or policy.

The bill establishes Youth Advisory Councils explicitly tasked with advising on climate change mitigation, resiliency, environmental justice, pollution reduction, and related environmental issues across multiple federal agencies. This directly advances expanded environmental protections and climate-focused policy.
While the bill references disadvantaged communities and environmental justice, it does not expand or modify welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net entitlements.
The bill creates youth advisory structures but does not address school funding, curriculum, choice, or federal education policy.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policies.
The bill contains no criminal justice, sentencing, or policing reforms.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions are present.
By authorizing new multi-year appropriations, the bill increases federal outlays and therefore works against prioritizing debt reduction.
The bill references diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility considerations under an existing executive order but does not create or expand specific legal protections for LGBTQ+ individuals.
The bill does not address foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions relate to voting access, election integrity, or electoral reforms.
The bill does not regulate technology, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
The bill does not address religious exemptions or conflicts between civil rights and religious liberty.
